question: Within the congenital anomalies of the abdominal wall are the omphalocele and gastroschisis. Both entities are defects of the wall. What is the difference between them?

options.opa: Omphalocele occurs at the umbilical level and gastroschisis at the epigastric level.
options.opb: The defect, in the case of gastroschisis, is larger than the omphalocele.
options.opc: In the omphalocele, a peritoneal sac covers the abdominal contents and not gastroschisis.
options.opd: Omphalocele, unlike gastroschisis, is frequently associated with intestinal atresia.
options.ope: Unlike the omphalocele, in gastroschisis the surgical treatment can be deferred.
